findings.title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
findings.body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of executing a query. Any existing consumer of `findMany` (e.g. insights tRPC handlers) will fail to compile / break at runtime. The PR contains no updates to callers, so either they exist and are broken, or the method is dead code; either way this needs to be verified and the call sites migrated in the same change.

findings.title: Constructor options type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
findings.body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId?: number` is optional for all scopes, instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with no `teamId` and it type-checks; zod validation then fails silently and `this.options` becomes null, so authorization conditions degrade to `1=0` and insights return empty results with no error surfaced. Keep the union type (or at least require teamId for team scope).

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` in the fallback cases), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This is misleading: a reader may assume auth conditions can be absent and that filters alone can be used, which would be a security hole if the auth path ever returned null. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter.

findings.title: toEqual against freshly-built Prisma.sql likely fails for composed SQL
findings.body: The service builds multi-part conditions by nesting templates (`Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})``), which produces a `Prisma.Sql` whose internal `strings`/`values` layout comes from flattening nested fragments. The test compares with `toEqual` against a single flat template literal containing the same final text. These objects are only deep-equal if the flattened `strings` array matches exactly; nesting typically yields different `strings` segmentation (and extra empty strings), so these assertions (team scope line 295, org scope line 332, combined filters line 429) will very likely fail. Compare `conditions.sql`/`text` and `conditions.values` instead, or run the SQL. The PR description itself admits the tests were never executed.

findings.title: Caching behaviour is no longer covered
findings.body: The two tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` memoize results were deleted, but the caching fields (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`, including the `undefined` vs `null` distinction for filters) still exist in the service. A regression where a `null` filter result is recomputed on every call, or where cached SQL is reused incorrectly, would now go undetected.
